chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) departed [for Mecca], a Bedouin met him at Al-Abtah and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I set out intending to perform Hajj, but I was hindered, and I am a man of means, meaning abundant wealth. So order me to do with my wealth what will allow me to achieve what the pilgrim achieves.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) turned towards Abu Qubays and said, 'If Abu Qubays were a pile of red gold for you, and you spent it in the way of Allah, you would not achieve what the pilgrim achieves.'

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: To depart or move from a place, specifically used for the Prophet's departure for Hajj
key_terms.الْأَبْطَح: A location near Mecca, between Mecca and Mina
key_terms.مَيِل: A man of means or wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of Hajj compared to spending all one's wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the unique spiritual status of Hajj by illustrating that even the expenditure of immense wealth cannot replicate its reward. The Prophet (SAWW) uses the metaphor of the mountain of Abu Qubays—located near Mecca—being turned into red gold to emphasize that the ritual act of pilgrimage holds a distinct merit that transcends material charity. This narrative is frequently cited by Shia scholars to highlight the incomparable value of performing Hajj at its prescribed time and place.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘When Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> departed, he<sup>saww</sup> came across a Bedouin at Al-Bat’ha, who said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I went out intending the Hajj but I was hindered, and I am an affluent man, meaning of abundant wealth. So order me to do (something) with my wealth by which I can achieve what I would achieve with by the Hajj’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> turned towards (Mount) Abu Qubays, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If (Mount) Abu Qubayys was (a pile of) red gold coins for you, spending it in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it would not achieve what the Hajj would achieve’.
en.sarwar: 25. Ali has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“He (the Imam) has said, that when the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, left an Arab came to him in al- Abtah and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I wanted to perform Hajj but something prevented me. I am a wealthy person. Command me to do something with my wealth that benefits me like the benefit of performing Hajj. The Messenger of Allah then looked to abu Qubays hill and said, “Even if you spend an amount of gold equal to the weight of abu Qubays hill for the cause of Allah, you will not gain the benefit of Hajj.’”
